title: MemoryItem
description: An inspectable, revisable machine-memory record (MEM). Memory is advisory and noncanonical until promoted into HKA through a governed AuthorityTransition. By default source_role is agent_memory, authority_state is noncanonical, and evidence_role excludes real-world `evidence`. A memory may support recall/context but must not be cited as factual evidence. Canonical standing is impossible without an explicit promotion + receipt reference. The semantic fields below ARE this object's metadata-bundle dimensions specialized for memory (object_type: memory_item).

scope_id.description: Scope this memory is bound to. Memory must be scoped; cross-scope recall requires a CrossScopeFlow.

source_role.description: Origin of the memory. Fixed to agent_memory — the canonical machine-memory source role — enforced as a constant (not a default annotation) so a memory can never validate as human/shared source material and thereby pass a CrossScopeFlow source_roles_allowed filter as if it were human-authored.

authority_state.description: Standing of the memory record — fixed to noncanonical. A memory is advisory and never holds draft/proposed/accepted/canonical/deprecated/etc. standing; promotion materializes a SEPARATE canonical artifact in HKA while this record stays noncanonical (MEM charter). Pinned as a const so a memory can never pass an authority_state filter intended for drafts, proposals, or canonical material.

evidence_role.description: What the memory may do in reasoning. Restricted to non-authoritative roles: memory is never real-world `evidence`. To carry factual evidence standing it must first be promoted into an HKA artifact.

derived_from.description: Source/provenance object IDs this memory was derived from.

invalid_at.description: Set when the memory is invalidated. Invalidation is distinct from suppression, tombstone, and purge stub.

memory_state.description: Coarse recall/existence lifecycle. Valid values are the memory-state axis in `_defs.schema.json#/$defs/memory_state`: unreviewed, reviewed, active, corrected, decayed, invalidated, forgotten, purged_stub. Promotion and visibility are tracked separately in `promotion_state` and `suppression_state`.

suppression_state.description: Visibility dimension. suppressed/tombstoned hide the memory from recall and context but never erase lineage/provenance. Distinct from invalidation and purge stub.

promotion_state.description: Governed-promotion sub-lifecycle. MEM may set promotion_requested; only GOV+HKA can reach promoted. promoted requires a promotion_request_id and an authority_receipt_ref.

promotion_request_id.description: Identifier of the promotion request / AuthorityTransition. Required once promotion_state is not not_requested.

authority_receipt_ref.description: AuthorityReceipt from the governed promotion. Required for any canonical authority_state and for promotion_state=promoted.

provenance_event_ids.description: ProvenanceEvent references; memory must carry provenance.

allOf.$comment: A purged stub has had its payload removed while lineage/provenance is retained; content must be empty so the purge cannot accidentally keep the original memory text.
Any promotion activity must carry the promotion request id.
A completed promotion must carry the governance receipt.
